title: Filtered-colimit continuity of derived functions on profinite parameters
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site with finite jointly surjective covering families, in the compatible universes of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Use ordinary internal modules and their ordinary unbounded derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. For a profinite set $P$, let $R[P]$ be the free internal $R$-module on $S\mapsto C(S,P)$, meaning the left adjoint of forgetting modules to condensed sets. Write $H_P(M)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R[P],M)$, the internal module Hom right adjoint to internal tensor, and derive it in its second variable by nonnegative injective resolutions [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $I$ be a small filtered category in the module universe and $M:I\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$ a diagram. Filtered means nonempty, every finite diagram admits a cocone. The canonical comparison is an isomorphism
$$\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I} RH_P(M_i[0])\longrightarrow RH_P((\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}M_i)[0])$$
in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_R)$. The left colimit is the exact filtered-colimit functor applied to a compatible diagram of complexes; equivalently its total left derived functor. The comparison is induced by the original coprojections $M_i\to\operatorname{colim}_iM_i$. It is natural in diagrams, continuous maps of profinite parameter sets, and morphisms of the supplied modules. No finite cohomological-dimension hypothesis on $P$ and no interchange of an unbounded product with a filtered colimit is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0GN3 (lemma-colim-global), applied to the coherent profinite slice sites; derived internal-function formulation by evaluating on profinite test sets.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=*_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ with the finite jointly surjective covering families specified in the statement. Products and covering pullbacks are profinite sets. A map into a profinite set descends uniquely along a finite jointly surjective family: the union of the sources is compact, the target is Hausdorff, and the surjection is a quotient map. Thus representables are sheaves. Sheafification on this site is strong symmetric monoidal for the objectwise tensor [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure], so the section-action equivalence $E$ from internal $R$-modules to module sheaves over the section ring [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] applies; it preserves underlying abelian sheaves, sections and maps. By [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] $E$ is symmetric monoidal from the relative tensor to $\otimes_R$. In $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ the right adjoint of $E(R[P])\otimes_R-$ is $\mathcal Hom_R(E(R[P]),-)$ [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], so uniqueness of right adjoints gives $E\circ H_P\cong\mathcal Hom_R(E(R[P]),-)\circ E$, naturally in $P$. As $E$ preserves underlying sheaves of sets, $E(R[P])$ is the free module sheaf on $h_P$, the sheafification of $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{h_P(V)}R(V)$. An equivalence preserves injectives and injective resolutions, so $E$ identifies the derived functors, the colimits and the comparison of the statement with those of $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. Write $F_i=UM_i$ and $F=U(\operatorname{colim}_i M_i)=\operatorname{colim}_iF_i$. The cited forgetful-functor theorem gives this equality and exactness of $U$. Exact filtered colimits of abelian sheaves then give exact filtered colimits of module sheaves: exactness is tested on the underlying abelian sheaves.

source.place: Tags 03DA (lemma-abelian), 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits), 03CO (lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves); profinite coherent topology as in sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring.

proof.text: For every $W\in\mathcal C$ and $q\geq0$, obtain $\operatorname{colim}_iH^q(W,F_i)\cong H^q(W,F)$ from the existing cohomology-of-colimit-sites theorem, as follows. Adjoin a strict initial object $o$ to $I$ and extend the coefficient diagram by $F_o=0$ and its unique maps. The resulting small category $I^+$ is filtered: any finite diagram with vertices in $I$ has a cocone there, and any added vertex $o$ has its unique arrow to that cocone; for a diagram consisting only of $o$, use any object of the nonempty $I$. Every cocone on the original diagram extends uniquely across the zero object, so its colimit is still $F$. On $(I^+)^{\mathrm{op}}$ take the constant system of sites $\mathcal C$ with identity transition functors. All coverings are finite; the colimit category and site of the cited construction are $\mathcal C$, because the index is nonempty and filtered. In the cohomology theorem choose the index $o$ and the object $W$. Its category of arrows $j\to o$ in $(I^+)^{\mathrm{op}}$ has exactly one such arrow for each $j$, so its filtered colimit is precisely the colimit over $I^+$. All site pullbacks are identities. The theorem therefore gives the displayed isomorphism with the actual coefficient coprojections, not just an abstract group isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09YP (lemma-colimit), applied to the constant finite-cover site system; sites.tex Tags 09YL (lemma-colimit-sites), 0A35 (lemma-compute-pullback-to-limit).

proof.text: Let $\iota$ be inclusion of abelian sheaves into presheaves, and for an abelian sheaf $G$ put $h^q(G)=H^q(R\iota(G[0]))$, an abelian presheaf. By the definition through injective resolutions, $h^q(G)(W)=H^q(W,G)$ for every $W$, naturally in $G$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], since kernels and cokernels of presheaves are computed objectwise; $h^q(G)=0$ for $q<0$ because the resolutions are nonnegative. Apply this to the coprojections $F_i\to F$. Presheaf colimits are computed objectwise, so the induced map $\operatorname{colim}_ih^q(F_i)\to h^q(F)$ is, at each $W$, exactly the isomorphism $\operatorname{colim}_iH^q(W,F_i)\to H^q(W,F)$ of step 2. Hence it is an isomorphism of abelian presheaves for every $q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This uses one fixed degree at a time and never takes a product over cohomological degrees.

source.place: Section 01FT (section-cohomology-sheaves), injective-resolution definition of object cohomology; algebra.tex Tag 00DB (lemma-directed-colimit-exact).

proof.text: Choose the compatible nonnegative injective resolutions $M_i\to I_i$, $M_\infty=\operatorname{colim}_iM_i\to I$ of the statement and let $c:\operatorname{colim}_iH_P(I_i)\to H_P(I)$ be the comparison. $U$ is exact, faithful and commutes with colimits [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], and a bijective $R$-linear sheaf map has an $R$-linear inverse; so $c$ is a quasi-isomorphism once $U(c)$ is. Exact filtered colimits of abelian sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact], applied to cycles, boundaries and their quotient, give $H^q(\operatorname{colim}_iUH_P(I_i))=\operatorname{colim}_iH^q(UH_P(I_i))$. Thus $H^q(Uc)$ is the map $\operatorname{colim}_iH^q(D(U)RH_P(M_i[0]))\to H^q(D(U)RH_P(M_\infty[0]))$ induced by the coprojections. Apply [lem-sfb-free-representable-derived-functions-model] with this $\mathcal C$, $R$, $P$: the site is small, has finite products and is subcanonical by step 1. Its isomorphism is natural in module maps and carries them to $D(a)D(t_P)R\iota$ of the underlying maps. As $a$ is exact [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] and $t_P$ is exact objectwise, $H^q$ commutes with both, giving isomorphisms $H^q(D(U)RH_P(M_i[0]))\cong a\,t_P\,h^q(F_i)$ natural in $i$ and compatible with the maps to $a\,t_P\,h^q(F)$. Since $a$ (a left adjoint) and $t_P$ (objectwise) commute with colimits, $H^q(Uc)$ is identified with $a\,t_P$ of the isomorphism of step 3. Both sides vanish for $q<0$. Hence $U(c)$ and $c$ are quasi-isomorphisms, and $c$ is invertible in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Only cohomology sheaves and the naturality of the model's isomorphisms are used; no lift of derived isomorphisms to a diagram of complexes is needed.

source.place: Tag 08J7 (section-internal-hom), via the derived-functions model; sites.tex Tag 00WJ (lemma-sheafification-exact); sites-modules.tex Tags 03DA, 03DB.

proof.text: All comparisons above are induced by the original coefficient coprojections. A morphism of diagrams commutes with each coprojection and hence with their induced map out of the colimit. For a continuous map $P'\to P$, the parameter restriction is induced by $W\times P'\to W\times P$; restriction of sections along this map commutes with every coefficient map $M_i\to M$. The derived-functions model is natural in both variables with this normalization, so these commuting squares remain commuting after passing to complexes, sheafification and the derived category. This proves the asserted naturality in diagrams, their module morphisms and profinite parameters.
